title: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 2 2024
description: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 2 2024 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: If a metal is heated sufficiently, it ______.
questions.explanation: This is a general scientific fact, so the zero conditional uses Present Simple in both clauses.

questions.questionText: If the laboratory temperature falls below the required level, the alarm ______ automatically.
questions.explanation: An automatic result is expressed with the zero conditional: Present Simple + Present Simple.

questions.questionText: Whenever the pressure increases beyond the limit, the safety valve ______.
questions.explanation: Whenever introduces a repeated general result, so Present Simple is required.

questions.questionText: If you ______ this switch, the system starts its emergency procedure.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes an automatic result, so the condition uses Present Simple.

questions.questionText: If the manager approves the proposal tomorrow, the company ______ the project next week.
questions.explanation: This is a realistic future possibility, so the first conditional is used.

questions.questionText: If you do not submit the application today, you ______ the deadline.
questions.explanation: A possible future consequence takes the first conditional: Present Simple + will + V1.

questions.questionText: If the weather improves this afternoon, we ______ the match.
questions.explanation: The condition is a realistic future possibility, so will is appropriate in the result clause.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: If the train will arrive early, we will leave.
If the train arrives early, we will leave.
If the train arrived early, we will leave.
If the train had arrived early, we will leave.
questions.explanation: In an ordinary first conditional, the if-clause uses Present Simple, not will.

questions.questionText: If you finish the report before noon, you ______ it to the director.
questions.explanation: A modal can may replace will in the result clause to express possibility or ability.

questions.questionText: If you are uncertain about the calculation, you ______ ask the instructor.
questions.explanation: Should in the result clause expresses advice.

questions.questionText: If the evidence is sufficient, the investigators ______ proceed with the case.
questions.explanation: May expresses possibility in the result clause.

questions.questionText: If you see the technician, ______ him to check the connection.
questions.explanation: A first conditional can have an imperative in the result clause.

questions.questionText: If the machine overheats, ______ it immediately.
questions.explanation: The result is an instruction, so an imperative is appropriate.

questions.questionText: If I ______ enough money, I would establish a free school.
questions.explanation: This is a hypothetical present situation, so the second conditional uses Past Simple.

questions.questionText: If she lived closer to campus, she ______ less time commuting.
questions.explanation: The condition is contrary to present reality, so the second conditional is required.

questions.questionText: If I ______ you, I would reconsider the decision.
questions.explanation: In formal English and examinations, were is preferred with I in hypothetical clauses.

questions.questionText: If the researcher ______ more confident, she would present the findings herself.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes a hypothetical present condition, requiring the second conditional.

questions.questionText: Which sentence expresses an unlikely future possibility?
options: If he studies tonight, he will pass.
If he studied tonight, he would improve his chances.
If he had studied, he would have passed.
If he studies regularly, he improves.
questions.explanation: Past Simple with would can express a hypothetical or unlikely present/future situation.

questions.questionText: If our team ______ more experienced, we would probably win the competition.
questions.explanation: The condition describes a hypothetical present characteristic, so were is used.

questions.questionText: If he ______ the necessary qualifications, he would apply for the position.
questions.explanation: The hypothetical present condition requires Past Simple.

questions.questionText: If I had known about the meeting, I ______ attended it.
questions.explanation: An unreal past result requires would have + V3.

questions.questionText: If they had left earlier, they ______ the beginning of the ceremony.
questions.explanation: The condition and result are both unreal past events, so the third conditional is required.

questions.questionText: If the driver had noticed the warning sign, the accident ______.
questions.explanation: An imagined past consequence takes would have + V3.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses an unreal past condition?
options: If I would have known, I would have acted.
If I knew, I would have acted.
If I had known, I would have acted.
If I have known, I would act.
questions.explanation: The third conditional requires If + Past Perfect and would have + V3.

questions.questionText: If she had not forgotten her passport, she ______ able to board the plane.
questions.explanation: The result refers to an unreal past event, so would have been is required.

questions.questionText: If we had taken a different route, we ______ the traffic yesterday.
questions.explanation: The condition and result both refer to an unreal past situation.

questions.questionText: If I had accepted that scholarship, I ______ at another university now.
questions.explanation: A past unreal condition produces a present result, making this a mixed conditional.

questions.questionText: If she had chosen engineering, she ______ an engineer now.
questions.explanation: The past decision affects the present situation, so Past Perfect + would + V1 is used.

questions.questionText: If I had saved more money when I was younger, I ______ financially secure now.
questions.explanation: A past condition with a present consequence forms a mixed conditional.

questions.questionText: If he were more organized, he ______ the deadline last week.
questions.explanation: A present characteristic is connected to an unreal past result, forming a mixed conditional.

questions.questionText: If I were more careful, I ______ that error yesterday.
questions.explanation: The present condition of being careful is linked to a past consequence.

questions.questionText: If he had studied medicine, he ______ a doctor now.
questions.explanation: The past educational choice has a present result, so this is mixed conditional type 1.

questions.questionText: Unless you ______ the instructions carefully, you will make mistakes.
questions.explanation: Unless already means if not, so another negative is normally unnecessary.

questions.questionText: Unless the weather improves, the match ______ cancelled.
questions.explanation: Unless introduces a real future condition, while the result uses will.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the correct use of unless?
options: Unless you don't hurry, you will miss the bus.
Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
Unless you will hurry, you miss the bus.
Unless you hurried, you will miss the bus.
questions.explanation: Unless already contains the meaning of if not.

questions.questionText: You may use the equipment ______ you follow all safety instructions.
questions.explanation: As long as means that the result is permitted provided the condition is satisfied.

questions.questionText: The organization will fund the project ______ it remains within the approved budget.
questions.explanation: Provided that introduces a condition that must be satisfied.

questions.questionText: You can stay here ______ you keep the room clean.
questions.explanation: As long as expresses a continuing condition or requirement.

questions.questionText: The student was allowed to enter the laboratory ______ he followed the safety regulations.
questions.explanation: On condition that means only if a particular condition is satisfied.

questions.questionText: You may borrow the equipment ______ you return it before Friday.
questions.explanation: Provided that introduces the required condition.

questions.questionText: Take a backup copy of the file ______ the computer crashes.
questions.explanation: In case expresses a precaution against a possible future event.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly distinguishes in case from if?
options: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
Take an umbrella in case it will rain.
In case it rains, we will definitely stay home.
In case means exactly the same as if.
questions.explanation: In case expresses preparation or precaution against a possible event.

questions.questionText: ______ the network fails, save your work locally as a precaution.
questions.explanation: In case is used when preparing for a possible future problem.

questions.questionText: Even if the examination is difficult, the students ______ continue working.
questions.explanation: Even if introduces a hypothetical condition whose occurrence will not change the result.

questions.questionText: Even though the examination was difficult, the students ______ working.
questions.explanation: Even though introduces a real known fact, not a hypothetical condition.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses even if?
options: Even if he is tired, he will finish the assignment.
Even if he was tired yesterday, he finished it.
Even if he had tired, he would finish.
Even if he would be tired, he will finish.
questions.explanation: Even if presents a hypothetical condition that does not change the expected result.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses even though?
options: Even though it may rain, we will play.
Even though it was raining, we played.
Even though it would rain, we played.
Even though it rains tomorrow, we played yesterday.
questions.explanation: Even though introduces a real fact, here the fact that it was raining.

questions.questionText: ______ you agree or not, the decision will remain unchanged.
questions.explanation: Whether ... or not means the result remains the same regardless of the condition.

questions.questionText: I will attend the meeting ______ the manager changes the schedule.
questions.explanation: Whether or not indicates that the result is independent of the condition.

questions.questionText: You may enter the examination hall ______ you have a valid admission card.
questions.explanation: Only if emphasizes that possessing the card is a necessary condition.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses inversion after only if?
options: Only if you work hard you will succeed.
Only if you work hard will you succeed.
Only if will you work hard succeed.
Only if you worked hard you will succeed.
questions.explanation: When only if begins the sentence, formal inversion places will before the subject in the main clause.

questions.questionText: A number is divisible by 2 ______ it is even.
questions.explanation: If and only if expresses a two-way necessary-and-sufficient relationship.

questions.questionText: ______ you provide the required documents, your application cannot be processed.
questions.explanation: Only if expresses a necessary condition.

questions.questionText: Suppose you ______ offered a place abroad. What would you do?
questions.explanation: Suppose introduces a hypothetical situation commonly followed by the second conditional.

questions.questionText: Supposing we ______ the last train, where would we stay?
questions.explanation: Supposing introduces an imagined situation, so Past Simple is appropriate for the second conditional.

questions.questionText: Assuming that the committee ______, we could begin the project next month.
questions.explanation: The sentence presents an imagined condition with a hypothetical result, so Past Simple fits the second conditional.

questions.questionText: If you ______ need further assistance, please contact the office.
questions.explanation: If + should expresses a possible but relatively unlikely future event in formal English.

questions.questionText: ______ you require additional information, please contact the administration.
questions.explanation: Should you require is the formal inverted equivalent of If you should require.

questions.questionText: If he should arrive before us, ______ him to wait.
questions.explanation: The conditional introduces a possible future event and the result is an imperative.

questions.questionText: If you happen to ______ David, please give him this message.
questions.explanation: If + happen to + V1 emphasizes an accidental or uncertain possibility.

questions.questionText: If you happen to ______ any problems, contact the support team.
questions.explanation: Happen to is followed by the base form of the verb in this conditional pattern.

questions.questionText: If I ______ more free time, I would learn another language.
questions.explanation: This expresses a hypothetical present situation, so the second conditional is required.

questions.questionText: I wish I ______ more confident when speaking in public.
questions.explanation: Wish + Past Simple expresses dissatisfaction or an unreal situation in the present.

questions.questionText: I wish I ______ the opportunity when it was offered.
questions.explanation: Wish + Past Perfect expresses regret about a past event.

questions.questionText: I wish you ______ making so much noise.
questions.explanation: Wish + would expresses a desire for another person's behavior or an annoying situation to change.

questions.questionText: If only I ______ enough money to continue my education.
questions.explanation: If only is a stronger form of wish; Past Simple expresses an unreal present condition.

questions.questionText: If only she ______ the warning before making the decision.
questions.explanation: A past regret requires Past Perfect after if only.

questions.questionText: Which sentence expresses regret about a past action?
options: I wish I had more time.
I wish I had studied harder.
I wish I would study harder.
questions.explanation: Wish + Past Perfect expresses regret about something that happened or failed to happen in the past.

questions.questionText: If you finish the assignment early, you ______ leave the classroom.
questions.explanation: Can in the result clause expresses permission or ability.

questions.questionText: If the weather becomes dangerous, the pilot ______ postpone the flight.
questions.explanation: May expresses possibility in the result clause.

questions.questionText: If you feel exhausted, you ______ take a short break.
questions.explanation: Should expresses advice.

questions.questionText: If employees repeatedly violate the rules, the organization ______ take disciplinary action.
questions.explanation: Must expresses necessity or a strong consequence.

questions.questionText: If he had asked for assistance, I ______ helped him.
questions.explanation: Could have expresses past ability or possibility in the result of an unreal past condition.

questions.questionText: If I ______ about the problem earlier, I could have helped you.
questions.explanation: The unreal past condition requires Past Perfect.

questions.questionText: Had I known about the change, I ______ prepared differently.
questions.explanation: Had I known is the inverted form of If I had known, so the result requires would have + V3.

questions.questionText: ______ I known the consequences, I would have refused the offer.
questions.explanation: Had + subject + V3 is the formal inversion of an if-clause with Past Perfect.

questions.questionText: ______ I were in your position, I would reconsider the proposal.
questions.explanation: Were I is the formal inverted equivalent of If I were.

questions.questionText: ______ you need any clarification, please contact the instructor.
questions.explanation: Should you need is the formal inversion of If you should need.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains correct conditional inversion?
options: Had I known, I would have acted.
Had I knew, I would have acted.
Did I know, I would have acted.
Would I known, I would have acted.
questions.explanation: The formal pattern is Had + subject + V3.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is the correct formal equivalent of 'If he were here, he would help us'?
options: Had he here, he would help us.
Were he here, he would help us.
Should he here, he would help us.
Would he be here, he would help us.
questions.explanation: Were + subject is the formal inversion of If + subject + were.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is the correct formal equivalent of 'If you should need assistance, call me'?
options: Should you need assistance, call me.
Had you need assistance, call me.
Were you need assistance, call me.
Would you need assistance, call me.
questions.explanation: Should + subject + V1 is the formal inverted form of If + subject + should + V1.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses conditional inversion incorrectly?
options: Had I known, I would have helped.
Were she here, she would understand.
Should you require assistance, contact us.
Did you study hard, you would pass.
questions.explanation: Ordinary Present Simple if-clauses cannot be inverted by simply removing if and using do or did.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an imperative as the result?
options: If you see the director, tell him immediately.
If you see the director, will tell him immediately.
If you saw the director, tell him immediately.
If you will see the director, tell him immediately.
questions.explanation: An imperative can directly follow a first conditional condition.

questions.questionText: If you finish the experiment, ______ the equipment carefully.
questions.explanation: The result is an instruction, so an imperative is used.

questions.questionText: If you feel unwell during the examination, ______ the supervisor.
questions.explanation: The conditional result is an imperative instruction.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has correct punctuation according to the standard school rule?
options: If you study hard you will pass.
If you study hard, you will pass.
If, you study hard you will pass.
If you study hard will, you pass.
questions.explanation: An initial if-clause is normally followed by a comma.

questions.questionText: Which sentence normally requires no comma between the two clauses?
options: If the weather improves, we will leave.
If you finish early, call me.
We will leave if the weather improves.
If he arrives late, we will start without him.
questions.explanation: When the main clause comes first, a comma is normally unnecessary.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?
options: You will succeed, if you work hard.
You will succeed if you work hard.
You will, succeed if you work hard.
You will succeed if, you work hard.
questions.explanation: The standard school rule normally omits the comma when the if-clause follows the main clause.

questions.questionText: Which sentence describes a general truth rather than a future possibility?
options: If you study tonight, you will pass.
If you heat ice, it melts.
If he arrives, we will begin.
If she calls, I will answer.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes an always-true result, so it is zero conditional.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is a first conditional?
options: If water reaches its boiling point, it boils.
If I were rich, I would travel.
If I study tonight, I will pass tomorrow.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes a realistic possible future condition and consequence.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is a second conditional?
options: If I had more time, I would learn another language.
If I have time, I will study.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
questions.explanation: Past Simple in the condition and would + V1 in the result indicate a hypothetical present/future situation.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is a third conditional?
options: If I were careful, I would avoid mistakes.
If I am careful, I will avoid mistakes.
If I had been careful, I would have avoided the mistake.
If I am careful, I avoid mistakes.
questions.explanation: Past Perfect plus would have + V3 expresses an unreal past situation.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is a mixed conditional?
options: If I study, I will pass.
If I studied, I would pass.
If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
questions.explanation: The past condition has a present result, creating a mixed time relationship.

questions.questionText: If the laboratory follows the safety rules, accidents ______ less likely.
questions.explanation: The sentence presents a possible future condition and result, so the first conditional is appropriate.

questions.questionText: If the laboratory followed stricter safety rules, accidents ______ less likely.
questions.explanation: The condition is hypothetical, so Past Simple + would + V1 is used.

questions.questionText: If the laboratory had followed stricter safety rules, the accident ______ prevented.
questions.explanation: This describes an unreal past condition and result.

questions.questionText: If the manager had invested in better equipment, the company ______ more efficient now.
questions.explanation: A past condition affects the present result, so this is a mixed conditional.

questions.questionText: If the company were more organized, it ______ the deadline last month.
questions.explanation: The present condition of being organized is linked to an unreal past consequence.

questions.questionText: Which option correctly completes the sentence? 'If I ______ the answer, I would tell you.'
questions.explanation: The result is hypothetical in the present, so the second conditional uses Past Simple.

questions.questionText: Which option correctly completes the sentence? 'If I ______ the answer yesterday, I would have told you.'
questions.explanation: The condition refers to an unreal past event, so Past Perfect is required.
